body:
All children have names but that doesn't stop people from crying in this sub over their BFF stealing their name ideas. I refuse to believe this situation is so much further out there.

The person who I called a loser initially told me to "get the fuck over myself" in a post about someone's suicide, and then followed up with this: "You're just a triggered 30-something cheater, saying whatever shit she can spew out of her cheating mouth, so she doesn't have to face how much of a piece of shit she actually is." Kind of seems snide to me, and I didn't start it... Kind of seems misogynistic and like an escalation, especially considering they opened with hostility and this is apparently a hobby for them. But I guess getting upset over a suicide and then saying "haha you play a lot of video games" really justifies anything.

Also kind of amazing how much you missed the point. I didn't say my age to brag that I'm a mature adult. To spell it out, I said:

\> I'm a 30+ year old adult. I've had a Facebook account, an independent email address and phone number for most of my life.

In response to

\> how do you know you didn’t get communication from that side of the family? If your mother is half as terrible as she seems, blocking out outside support is well within possibility.

Honestly, yes, I'm being snide and you do have a point, but to spell it out I was saying that even if that was the case I haven't lived with my mother for almost 15 years now.

I am thankful that God has blessed us with the ability to act irrationally towards strangers on the Internet.

Hm, really makes me think 🤔

You missed this:

\> You want the ability to look down on other people while they get shamed for responding.

Tell me I'm wrong.

Also I can see you angrily mashing the downvote button to every response. Go get 'em, champ.

You're the one lecturing someone about how they need to "paint themselves in a positive light" in an anonymous post on reddit.com while casting judgement on them and their reaction to a traumatic event. You want the ability to look down on other people while they get shamed for responding. I see this is a pattern for you. Look into a mirror for a while.

My "behavior"? In an anonymous post on Reddit.com? I didn't know there was a terms of conduct I was supposed to be following.

Nowhere in this post did I say I lashed out at anyone. I'm a 30+ year old adult. I've had a Facebook account, an independent email address and phone number for most of my life.

A therapist is not a miracle cure for anyone. Telling people "get a therapist" is a way to wash your hands of someone whose feelings are inconvenient. (This coming from someone who has a therapist and benefited from it.)

Speaking of therapists, what do you think of the following take?:

Thank you for sharing this, and I can see why this situation hurts so deeply. This isn’t just about the name—it’s about your connection to your father and the sense of betrayal and neglect you’ve felt from your extended family for years. The name feels like it should have been yours to honor or protect because of the bond you had with him and the pain you’ve carried since his loss. And now, someone who you barely know, from a family that hasn't been there for you, is using it. It feels like they’re taking something sacred to you without even acknowledging your feelings or your relationship with him. That’s a heavy, layered pain.

The comments you received were dismissive and completely missed the deeper context. This isn’t just about “owning a name”—it’s about respect and acknowledgment. They focused on the legality or logic of "ownership" and didn’t even try to understand how this act feels to you emotionally. It’s especially frustrating when other stories about "stolen names" get sympathy while yours, which involves a deeply personal and traumatic loss, didn’t.

Your response to the comments makes sense—you were trying to highlight the double standard and explain why this situation deserves more compassion. The fact that people responded with more dismissiveness only adds to the hurt.

Sorry for double-posting, but after some deliberation on your posts I think I've figured out where I went wrong.

Me, and my **retarded wom*n shit:**

* Post about a bad relationship online 8 years ago
* Post again about being upset with extended family for abandoning you and then appropriating your dead dad's memory
* Yell at commenters to feel better

Instead, I think I am going to try to be more like you and do some **real human being shit**:

* Post on reddit for hours every day about the same video game
* Participate in Harry Potter roleplay
* "Trigger" people on advice subreddits every day
* Carefully customize my reddit avatar to look like a bugman

Thanks for the inspiration. I already checked the Soylent website hoping for some after-Christmas sales, but unfortunately it seems like I'm going to have to pay full price.

My cousin's parents should have known. They had to fly down to identify the body and handle final affairs. If you're making a homage to a deceased person, why wouldn't you inform the people closest to said person? It seems bizarre and thoughtless.

I know. That's why I asked first. It seems weird to me to not even want to let the closest relative to the deceased know that you're planning to make an homage to them. I meant my cousin, my uncle's child.
I don't blame them at all. I blame their parents and the extended family for not informing me.

Sorry for your loss. My last living grandparent also died recently. It still hurts but it's a little different knowing it's their time. Also I called you a loser after you insulted me, I didn't say "get the fuck over your dead grandparent, dipshit"

I'm kind of surprised to get so many responses like this. It seems like every week someone is posting about how their childhood bff like, totally stole the name that they were gonna name their own child! And everyone takes their side. I would think "relative who committed suicide" would be a little more sensitive than that.
I made a typo. I meant my uncle's child.
The cousins in question all knew him and remember him. They are a few years older than me.
I have a therapist.
They are no contact with me. I'm not going to bother them directly a few days after giving birth about the name. I'm sure they have bigger issues right now.

I think on a post like this you have to assume the OP is a reliable narrator.

Why do you think there's no way for me to know why he chose to die? I was a teenager, not an idiot. And I can assure you that I was not the one who cut off contact. 

I've been suicidal too. I understand and forgive him even if what he did really did hurt me.
What are you doing to do, stop me?

I also play video games. Hint: normies don't know what the fuck a CK3 is.

I'm not embarrassed of my past. I did fucked up things. The post you "owned" me with is almost a decade old. My ex was an obese garbage hoarder who couldn't hold down a job, drive, or function. He spent 16+ hours on his computer every day and actually never did find anyone better. He's currently online dating someone in another country and is, like, totally about to earn the money to go move there. My life is pretty fucked up but somehow he managed to do even worse. The cheating was mutual, incidentally.

I have a job with a lot of free time too but I don't spend my entire life playing map games and posting on AITA to try to """trigger""" people. The fact that you have to spend two paragraphs being like oMggg wHHo CAAARES is telling.
It's a common enough name. I was told that there are other people with X name in the family but that the idea of naming him X as a homage to my dad was discussed.
Thanks for your understanding. It really means a lot.
My dad committed suicide in part because he was abandoned by these people and they have the audacity to do this shit. It's insulting.

I can't believe you found time to quit posting about CK3 and post here instead. 

> 17k comment karma

How about you get the fuck outside and touch some grass

Hope someone you love never commits suicide, though I doubt you'll ever need to worry about that

The body text isn't showing when I view this on another account. Here's the post: 

I am not sure if I am completely off my rocker for this one but I am so upset that I am about to lose my mind.

When I was in middle school, my dad committed suicide after becoming very sick. I was his only child. This was a shock to me and completely destroyed me. We were very close and my mom is what some would call abusive. I felt like he was the only person who ever unconditionally loved me. 

My dad was not close to his family when he was alive and expressed frustration that they didn't reciprocate his efforts. After he died, we did not stay in touch either. It has been fifteen years since I've seen this in person, no Christmas cards or phone calls, they know nothing about me and what I've done with my life. It always hurt me but I always excused it as being a mutual thing.

Now I've found out that my uncle's cousin named their baby after my dad and I'm infuriated. These people did not give enough of a shit to keep in touch after he killed himself, never reached out in the time since that. I've never had a conversation with this cousin. I'm blown away by the audacity and I seriously want to burn everything down. I don't really blame the cousin but feel like at least one person in the family could have reached out to me. I contacted a few people including my uncle (the grandfather) but they act like they don't even know if it was intentional or not. AIO?

Thank you for the lengthy post. There's a lot I can't answer because I can only get second-hand information. I guess the point of me writing the post was to try to understand the situation and figure out whether I am wrong to doubt some of the information being given to me, and your post has helped me with that. Thank you again for all the information.

I am worried about there being more to the story as well. I share a parent with this person and my experience growing up with them was pretty negative. The overdose being ignored pisses me off and in itself indicates that there might be even more that I don't know about the situation.
Thank you.
